content.user_title: Manage Azure Key Vault Secrets in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need safe patterns for storing and retrieving sensitive configuration. This skill explains Azure Key Vault Secrets SDK workflows for clients, secret operations, rotation, backup, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Explains Maven dependency setup for the Azure Key Vault Secrets Java SDK.
Shows how to create SecretClient and SecretAsyncClient with DefaultAzureCredential.
Covers set, get, list, update, delete, recover, purge, backup, and restore operations.
Demonstrates loading multiple named secrets into Java configuration maps.
Describes a secret rotation pattern using new secret versions and property updates.
Summarizes common error handling for missing secrets, access denial, and rate limits.
limitations: It does not provision Azure Key Vault, managed identities, RBAC, or network rules.
It does not validate examples against a live Azure tenant or vault.
It covers Key Vault secrets, not Key Vault keys or certificates.
Several source examples need production hardening for logging and placeholder secret values.

use_cases.title: Add Secret Retrieval to a Java Service
use_cases.description: Use the SDK patterns to connect a Java application to Azure Key Vault and retrieve named configuration secrets.

use_cases.title: Plan a Rotation Workflow
use_cases.description: Design a process for creating new secret versions, disabling old versions, and checking expiry metadata.

use_cases.title: Document Recovery Operations
use_cases.description: Prepare operational guidance for deleting, recovering, purging, backing up, and restoring Key Vault secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Key Vault Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Java service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create a Java client for Azure Key Vault Secrets using DefaultAzureCredential. Keep secret values out of logs.

prompt_templates.title: Replace Hardcoded Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Move application settings into Azure Key Vault.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me replace hardcoded configuration with Azure Key Vault Secrets in a Java service. Include retrieval, missing-secret handling, and safe logging.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secret Rotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secret rotation workflow for a Java service using Azure Key Vault Secrets. Include version handling, expiry metadata, rollback, and monitoring checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Secret Management Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Java Key Vault secret-management plan for security gaps. Check access control, logging, backup and restore, purge behavior, async handling, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: Review my plan for retrieving database credentials from Azure Key Vault in a Java service.
output: The client setup uses managed Azure identity and a vault URL from configuration.
Secret values are not printed or returned in diagnostics.
Add handling for missing secrets, access denial, and rate limiting.

output_examples.input: Create a checklist for rotating an API key stored in Key Vault.
output: Create a new secret version and set an expiration date.
Update consumers to read the current version by name.
Disable the old version after validation and keep rollback notes.

output_examples.input: Summarize backup and recovery guidance for Key Vault secrets.
output_examples.output: Back up important secrets before destructive changes, test restore in a controlled vault, and document purge permissions separately.

best_practices: Use managed identity or another approved Azure credential flow instead of embedding credentials in source code.
Log only secret names, versions, and operation status, never secret values.
Set expiration, ownership tags, and access policies that match each environment.
anti_patterns: Do not print secret values during retrieval, listing, error handling, or async callbacks.
Do not paste real passwords, API keys, or connection strings into examples or prompts.
Do not purge deleted secrets unless recovery requirements and retention rules are satisfied.

faq.question: Does this skill create an Azure Key Vault?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Java SDK usage after a vault and identity configuration already exist.

faq.question: Which Java packages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers azure-security-keyvault-secrets and uses azure-identity for DefaultAzureCredential client authentication.

faq.question: Does it include synchronous and asynchronous clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SecretClient and SecretAsyncClient patterns for common secret operations.

faq.question: Can it help with secret rotation?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes creating a new version, updating properties, and disabling older versions.

faq.question: Does it cover keys or certificates?
faq.answer: No. It is limited to Key Vault secrets and related secret properties.

faq.question: Is the guidance production ready as written?
faq.answer: Not fully. Users should remove value logging, replace sample secrets, and verify Azure permissions before production use.
